title: Tool Design for AI Agents: Why Fewer, Sharper Tools Always Win #tech #agent
description:
The agents that perform best are not the ones with the most tools. They are the ones with the fewest, sharpest tools designed to make the right choice obvious.

Three rules that separate good tool design from bad. Granularity first. Do not give the agent fifty narrow tools that all do slightly different things. 

Consolidate them. Instead of separate tools for pulling customer data, orders, and payments, build one tool that returns everything at once. Less choosing means fewer mistakes. Names second. The agent picks tools by reading their names so the name has to be self-explanatory. 

Send email to customer tells the agent exactly what it does. Action one tells it nothing. Clean error messages third. When a tool fails the agent needs to know why so it can decide what to do next. Customer not found is actionable. Error 404 is not.

The agent is not what makes a great agent look smart. The toolset is.
